title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of risankizumab in multirefractory Crohn’s disease: A multicenter AIRIS-Crohn registry analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND Many patients with Crohn’s disease (CD) remain uncontrolled despite multiple biologic therapies. Risankizumab, a selective interleukin-23p19 inhibitor, has shown efficacy in clinical trials, but real-world data in multirefractory CD are still scarce. AIM To evaluate the 12-month effectiveness and safety of risankizumab in a real-world cohort of patients with moderate-to-severe CD treated across multiple centers in Andalusia, Spain. METHODS Multicenter ambispective real-world study including adults with CD treated with risankizumab across 12 Andalusian hospitals (AIRIS-Crohn registry). Effectiveness outcomes were clinical remission (Harvey-Bradshaw index < 5), steroid-free remission (SFR), biochemical remission, and endoscopic response/remission at week 12, 6 months and 12 months. Modified non-responder imputation was applied to discontinuations. RESULTS Among 205 patients with highly refractory CD (median 2 prior failed advanced therapies; 81% prior ustekinumab exposure; 61% extraintestinal manifestations; 39% prior intestinal surgery), risankizumab rapidly improved clinical activity and maintained stable remission rates over 12 months. Clinical remission improved from 20% at baseline to 49% at week 12, 46% at 6 months and 49% at 12 months (P < 0.05 for all). SFR was maintained in 41%-44% throughout follow-up. Perianal disease response was observed in 65% at week 12 and 80% at 6 months. Endoscopic remission was achieved in 32% at 6 months. Treatment persistence exceeded 90% at one year. In multivariable analysis, prior vedolizumab exposure was related to lower odds of SFR (odds ratio = 0.41; 95% confidence interval: 0.17-0.99). Risankizumab demonstrated a reassuring safety profile: Only 3.4% of patients discontinued due to adverse events, and no serious infections, opportunistic infections, malignancies, or deaths occurred during follow-up. CONCLUSION In one of the largest real-world cohorts of multirefractory CD, risankizumab delivered rapid and sustained clinical benefit, meaningful SFR, robust treatment persistence, and a reassuring safety profile. These findings strengthen the role of interleukin-23 blockade as a key therapeutic strategy for patients with limited treatment options in everyday practice.

title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
journal: Journal of Asian Multicultural Research for Economy and Management Study
abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

title: Transformasi Akuntansi Manajemen pada Era Artificial Intelligence: Tinjauan Literatur Terstruktur tentang Efisiensi, Pengendalian Biaya, dan Pengambilan Keputusan Management Accounting Transformation in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Structured Literature Review on Efficiency, Cost Control, and Decision-Making
journal: AL-IMAM: Journal on Islamic Studies, Civilization and Learning Societies
abstract: Aim: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in four core management accounting functions: cost analysis, budgeting, management control, and decision-making. Method: A structured literature review synthesizes findings from systematic reviews, case studies, experiments, a dissertation, and professional reports to distinguish demonstrated predictive benefits from broader claims about organizational performance. The review is limited by the absence of a complete database export and a study-specific PRISMA flow; it should therefore be read as a structured synthesis of accessible literature rather than a fully reproducible systematic review. Results: Machine-learning models can match or exceed human estimates in selected cost-estimation tasks when adequate historical data are available. In budgeting, machine learning can improve prediction accuracy, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causal effects or guarantee appropriate resource allocation. In management control, digital tools support more timely and anticipatory monitoring, although the available evidence does not always isolate the effect of AI itself. For decision-making, the usefulness of AI depends on data quality, model explainability, user trust, professional competence, and the preservation of human accountability. Novelty/Implications: The novelty lies in organizing the evidence by management accounting function and strength of evidence, separating technical outcomes (prediction accuracy) from organizational outcomes. AI is best positioned as support for professional judgment rather than a replacement for management accountants. Organizations need data governance, model evaluation, and training to ensure responsible adoption, and the article proposes an empirical research agenda, particularly in Indonesian organizations, on AI use, efficiency, cost control, and decision quality.

title: Thermal response during erbium laser-assisted removal of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract This review aimed to systematically map and synthesize the available evidence regarding the thermal effects of laser-assisted debonding of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers on the dental pulp and to identify current knowledge gaps. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the scoping review was conducted after preliminary screening identified limited and heterogeneous evidence for a systematic review. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two independent reviewers screened eligible studies and extracted data on laser parameters, irradiation protocols, restorative characteristics, debonding performance, and thermal outcomes. A total of 63 records were identified, and 10 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this scoping review. Er, Cr: YSGG was the most investigated laser, followed by Er: YAG. The included studies evaluated the debonding of lithium disilicate and zirconia laminate veneers and full-coverage crowns. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in laser parameters, ceramic materials, restoration thicknesses, and outcome assessment methods. Intrapulpal temperature change and debonding time were the most frequently reported outcomes, with most studies reporting temperature increases below the commonly cited historical thermal threshold for irreversible pulp damage. Current evidence suggests that erbium laser-assisted debonding can be associated with temperature increases within the pulp chamber, with the magnitude of the thermal response varying according to laser parameters, cooling protocols, and restorative characteristics. However, the lack of standardized experimental protocols, standardized control groups, and clinical evidence prevents definitive conclusions regarding pulpal safety or the establishment of evidence-based clinical recommendations.

title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
journal: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction showed the strongest association with Customer Loyalty (β = 0.494) and partially mediated both upstream paths (indirect effects β = 0.269 and β = 0.229). The study empirically extends the satisfaction-mediation framework to regulated B2B outsourcing and indicates that satisfaction management should be the central lever in loyalty-building strategy.

title: The Influence of Profitability, Interest Rates (BI Rate) and Institutional Ownership on Stock Returns at PT Akasha Wira Internasional Tbk
abstract: This study examines the relationships between profitability, the Bank Indonesia policy interest rate, institutional ownership, and stock returns at PT Akasha Wira International Tbk over the 2013–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from the company’s annual reports and Bank Indonesia publications. The dataset comprises 12 annual observations. Profitability was measured using return on assets (ROA), while institutional ownership was measured by the proportion of shares held by institutional investors. The interest-rate variable was based on Bank Indonesia’s published policy-rate series, taking into account changes in the official benchmark terminology during the observation period. Multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing were conducted using SPSS version 23. The results indicate that profitability is positively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = 4.476, p = 0.002), whereas the policy interest rate is negatively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = −2.830, p = 0.022). Institutional ownership does not exhibit a statistically significant partial association with stock returns (t = 1.803, p = 0.109). Simultaneously, the three independent variables are statistically significant in the regression model (F = 10.610, p = 0.004). The model yields an R-squared of 0.799, indicating that the predictors jointly account for 79.9% of the in-sample variation in stock returns, while the adjusted R-squared is 0.724 after accounting for the number of predictors and observations. Given the limited sample and single-company setting, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. This study provides case-specific evidence concerning the relationships between firm-level profitability, monetary policy, ownership structure, and stock returns

Organising under uncertainty: how startup investors construct value through sensemaking
journal: Qualitative Research in Organizations and Management: An International Journal
abstract: Purpose This study examines how early-stage investors construct startup value under conditions of uncertainty. Drawing on a sensemaking perspective, it explores how investors interpret and integrate resource, leadership and contextual cues into coherent valuation judgements of venture potential. Design/methodology/approach Utilising a semi-structured interview approach, qualitative data were generated from seven startup investors in Malaysia, capturing experiential reflections and evaluative reasoning. An iterative interpretive analysis was conducted, with computational text analysis used for supplementary pattern-checking and visualisation. The themes are presented as interconnected dimensions of investors' valuation narratives. Findings The findings illustrate that valuation is constructed through a dynamic sensemaking process in which investors integrate five interrelated dimensions: operational discipline, customer and market focus, technological capability, product–market viability and team and leadership. Investors complement available financial information with interpretive narratives that connect internal capabilities, leadership and external conditions into coherent assessments of venture potential. Leadership emerges as the central integrative mechanism, while early customer validation anchors credibility. Valuation therefore emerges as an ongoing negotiation between uncertainty and conviction. Originality/value The study extends startup valuation research by explaining how investors complement available financial indicators with interpretive sensemaking when constructing valuation judgements under uncertainty. It further shows how resources, leadership and ecosystem conditions are integrated into coherent valuation narratives.
